culture.name: THE CROWN
culture.what: A physical crown (or belt) that moves to every Battle winner. It sits on his desk all week.

culture.name: THE BELL
culture.what: Every sale rings the bell in the office and gets a post in #bell on Discord. No sale goes unheard.

culture.name: WALKOUT SONGS
culture.what: Every agent picks one. Battle contestants walk out to theirs.

culture.name: BOUNTY BOARD
culture.what: Daily bounties from leadership: first sit before 10, most dials by lunch, first IUL of the week.

culture.name: DRAFT DAY
culture.what: Captains snake-draft teams for the next week's Throw-Down competition.

culture.name: SHARK TANK
culture.what: 60-second recruiting pitches scored by a 3-person panel. It builds the agency-building muscle.

culture.name: REVERSE ROLE PLAY
culture.what: Leaders play the agent and agents play the nightmare client. The room learns by watching the pros get tested.

culture.name: GUEST MIC
culture.what: Once a month, an outside top producer or agency owner joins on Zoom for a 20-minute Q&A.

culture.name: THE CROWNING CEREMONY
culture.what: The last Saturday of each month is the awards show. Dress up, give speeches, hand out trophies.

research.steal: Ask questions that let the client talk himself into the problem: Connect → Situation → Problem → Solution → Consequence → Commit. Curious tone, no pushing.
The client must rate the product, you, and the company a 10 out of 10 on certainty. Tonality carries certainty. Loop objections back to certainty instead of arguing.
Labels ("It sounds like…"), mirrors (repeat their last 1–3 words), an accusation audit that names their fears first, and "how/what" questions. Go for "That's right" instead of "You're right."
Clarify, Label, Overview past pain, Sell the vacation, Explain away concerns, Reinforce. Every objection is circumstances, other people, or self. Rule of 100: 100 primary actions a day for 100 days.
The 30-Day Rule: today's prospecting pays off over the next 90 days. Protect your Golden Hours for selling only. For brush-offs, use Ledge → Disrupt → Ask.

research.what: Daily reps and high-standard sales culture
research.steal: Role play every single day, loud and in front of the room. Standards and energy are trained like skills.
Set targets 10× bigger and match them with massive action. Most people fail from too little activity, not too much.
Persistency is the business: match draft dates to deposit days, sell a premium they can keep, and follow up before the first draft.
Follow-up and personal brand compound. Post daily, show receipts, and treat your book of business like a company.

data.text: Contact is 100× more likely when you call within 5 minutes instead of 30 (MIT / InsideSales Lead Response Management study).
Openers that state a reason for the call perform about 2× better. "Is this a bad time?" cuts results by roughly 40% (Gong Labs cold-call research).
LIMRA has long reported that only about 1 in 7 new agents is still in the business four years later. Culture and training are the retention plan.
The chargeback window. A lapse inside it comes out of your pocket and can cost you carrier contracts.

compliance: Calling hours: federal law allows 8 AM–9 PM in the client's local time. Florida is stricter at 8 AM–8 PM, and it limits repeat solicitation calls to the same person within 24 hours. Check each state with your IMO or compliance before dialing late.
Recording: Florida requires every party's consent to record a call. Only use disclosed and consented recordings in the Film Room.
No rebating: the reward card goes out whether the client buys or not. Sale posts show the client's first name and last initial only.
